meta.label: looseness
meta.reason: Query shows high 1x on all 4 channels 0.011-0.016, ruling out normal (~0.0003-0.0016) and misalignment (1x ~0.0003-0.0012, 2x-dominant). 1x dominance alone suggests unbalance vs looseness. Unlike unbalance references where 1x >>2x e.g. 0.0137 vs 0.0019, 0.0126 vs 0.0050, 0.0178 vs 0.0052, query has substantial harmonics: ch0 1x 0.0116, 2x 0.0089, 3x 0.0115 (1x/3x ~1.0) and ch2 1x 0.0159, 2x 0.0130, 3x 0.0032 (1x/2x ~1.2). This multi-harmonic elevation with 1x still high matches looseness references e.g. 1x 0.0075/2x 0.0077/3x 0.0048 and 1x 0.0142/2x 0.0131/3x 0.0242. Limitation: radial signals and one short recording cannot uniquely separate unbalance with secondary looseness, but harmonic pattern favors looseness over pure unbalance.

superseded_study.reason: Harmonic bands were centred on the nominal 1238 RPM (20.63 Hz). The recordings actually run at about 1260-1302 RPM (21.0-21.7 Hz), so the 3x band (60.4-63.4 Hz) missed the 3x peak near 65 Hz and the 2x band caught only its edge. Found in code review on 2 Nov 2026 after the results were recorded.

limitations: Shaft speed is estimated from each recording's spectrum; the documented ~1238 RPM did not match where the harmonics are. An earlier study (real-1) that used 1238 RPM is kept and reported as superseded.
Real accelerometer measurements from a laboratory rig with deliberately introduced faults; not a live factory installation.
One preselected one-second window per test; only eight held-out trials from one rig.
No temperature, force, newly commanded speed/load experiment or calibrated fault probability is available.
Reference and test trials are separated by source test, not windows from the same recording.
The baseline uses all four channels; Meta may inspect fewer. This is not a controlled equal-information comparison.
Native amplitude units are not verified; no conversion to g, displacement or engineering alarm threshold is claimed.
